headline: Texas Coal Plant Becomes Gateway for Massive Solar Expansion
meta_description: Energy firm invests $1.7B to build 1.2 GW solar complex next to Texas coal plant, reusing existing grid infrastructure for clean energy delivery.
summary_short: A $1.7 billion solar project in Robertson, Texas will leverage an aging coal plant's grid connections to deliver renewable power to millions.
body:
Energy investment firm Panamint is investing $1.7 billion to construct Big Rooter Power, a massive solar-storage complex in Robertson, Texas that will add 1.2 gigawatts of solar capacity to the regional grid. Rather than develop new land, the project takes strategic advantage of existing infrastructure at the Twin Oaks coal-fired plant, demonstrating how aging fossil fuel sites can become gateways for renewable energy expansion. "We believe deploying new capacity at existing energy sites is the clearest way to benefit communities, ratepayers, and the environment alike," said Apolka Totth, CEO of Panamint.

Big Rooter reflects a growing national trend: repurposing brownfields—previously developed industrial or extractive sites—for solar and wind projects. This approach costs significantly less than developing undeveloped land. Similar projects are already underway or completed in Illinois, Kentucky, and Louisiana on reclaimed mine land. The strategy allows developers to maximize existing grid connections, transmission lines, and electrical infrastructure while avoiding the expense of new site preparation.

The project will unfold in two stages. Construction has already begun on the first phase, which will bring 491 megawatts of solar panels online by August 2028. The second phase, breaking ground in December 2028, will add the remaining 658 megawatts by August 2029, accompanied by 1.6 gigawatts of battery storage and 20 miles of new high-transmission power lines. Long lead-time equipment like transformers and circuit breakers have already been ordered, taking advantage of available tax incentives. The project is expected to qualify for a Federal investment tax credit covering 50 percent of costs. Once complete, Big Rooter will rank among the nation's largest solar installations.
quick_facts: Panamint investing $1.7 billion in Robertson, Texas solar project
1.2 gigawatts of solar power added to grid by 2029
First phase delivers 491 MW by August 2028
Project qualifies for 50% Federal investment tax credit
Reuses existing Twin Oaks coal plant grid infrastructure
